reason: Gehazi (גֵּיחֲזִי) is an explicitly named character in this passage, identified as 'the servant of Elisha, man of God' (נַעַר אֱלִישָׁע אִישׁ־ הָאֱלֹהִים). He is not a leader but rather a subordinate servant/attendant to the prophet Elisha. He performs tasks at Elisha's direction and is later struck with leprosy as punishment for his greedy pursuit of gifts from Naaman. While the other named characters (Naaman, Elisha, and the kings) are indeed leaders, Gehazi demonstrates that not all named characters occupy leadership positions.
